claim: The enum formatter template has its preprocessor guard inverted: `#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK`, while every other template uses `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. On modern targets (net6/net8 and others), generated enum formatters are not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The attribute appears only on the targets the change itself treats as unsupported. This breaks the acceptance criterion that all generated code is decorated.

claim: EnumTemplate uses the inverted guard `#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK`, while every other template uses `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. claim: The preprocessor condition in EnumTemplate is inverted relative to every other template. The attribute is emitted only when NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK is defined, which are exactly the targets where the attribute is assumed unavailable. Enum formatters therefore get no exclusion on modern targets, so the requirement is unmet for them. On netstandard2.0/net472 the attribute is emitted, which may fail to compile there if ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is absent; it exists in netstandard2.0 and net40+, so it is probably fine on those targets. The result is an inconsistent and incorrect guard.
